raw_case_text:
A 50-year-old male, presented with complaints of fever and extensive rashes on the skin of the face and the neck, ulcerations and erythema of the conjunctiva and the oral cavity and difficulty in swallowing, of ten days' duration. The past medical history of the patient revealed that he had been diagnosed with HIV infection (HIV-1) eight months back. He was initiated on HAART therapy (zidovudine 300 mg + lamivudine 150 mg + NVP 200 mg) a month back when the viral load was 1, 09,000 copies/ml. The patient was also on anti-tuberculosis treatment (ATT) (rifampacin 150 mg, isoniazid 300 mg) and vitamin supplements for the past three months. The patient was well-oriented and on examination, had hyperpyrexia, generalized, maculopapular and bullous eruptions on the neck, face and the trunk [Figures 1 and 2]. Intraorally, the patient was completely edentulous and had multiple oral ulcers of the buccal mucosa, soft palate and buccal vestibule. The ulcers were hemorrhagic and tender on palpation. Hemorrhagic erosions were also seen on both the upper and lower lips [Figures 1 and 2]. Ophthalmic examination showed acute conjunctivitis and subconjunctival hemorrhages. There was no history of previous hypersensitivity reaction to drugs. The pruritis involving the oral and the ocular region was followed by vesicles and ulcerations four days after the initiation of HAART therapy.
The laboratory investigations at the time of admission to our referral centre showed a CD4 count of 470 cells/microliter (normal range 200-1347 cells/microliter), total white blood cell (WBC) count was 4860-cells/cu mm (normal range 4000-11000 cells/cu mm), hemoglobin 11.9 g/dl (normal range 12-17 g/dl) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 36 mm/h (normal range 0-14mm/h). The platelet count was 208 x 109/L (normal range 137-367 x 109/L) and random blood glucose was 186 mg/dl (normal range 80-120 mg/dl). Urine analysis and serum chemistry were within normal limits. A chest radiograph of the patient did not show any active tuberculous lesion.
On the basis of the history and clinical presentation a diagnosis of SJS was made. As the first line of treatment HAART was discontinued and the patient was administered intravenous 5% dextrose and 2 ml dexamethasone (4 mg/ml). Supportive therapy with oral topical anesthetic gel (lignocaine 2%) for the oral ulcers was prescribed. The ocular lesions were managed with dexamethasone (0.1%) eye drops and crusting dry lesions were managed with liquid paraffin. The skin and the oral lesions healed over a period of two weeks. The patient was subsequently followed up and after 12 weeks the oral mucosal lesions resolved completely [Figures 3 and 4].

subjective.chief_complaint: A 50-year-old HIV-positive male presented with a 10-day history of fever, extensive facial, neck, and truncal blistering skin rash, ocular redness, hemorrhagic oral and labial ulcerations, and dysphagia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed with HIV-1 infection 8 months prior and treated with anti-tuberculosis therapy for 3 months, the patient was initiated on HAART (zidovudine 300 mg + lamivudine 150 mg + nevirapine 200 mg) 1 month prior to presentation. Four days after starting HAART, he developed oral and ocular pruritus that rapidly progressed over the next 10 days to high fever, generalized maculopapular and bullous skin eruptions, acute conjunctivitis, painful hemorrhagic oral and lip ulcers, and severe dysphagia.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV-1 infection diagnosed 8 months prior (baseline viral load 109,000 copies/mL 1 month prior); pulmonary/systemic tuberculosis on anti-tuberculosis therapy for the past 3 months. No prior history of drug hypersensitivity.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, oral/ocular pruritus, dysphagia, painful oral/lip ulcers, ocular redness, and blistering skin rash. Home medications: zidovudine 300 mg, lamivudine 150 mg, nevirapine 200 mg (started 1 month prior), rifampicin 150 mg, isoniazid 300 mg, and vitamin supplements.

objective.physical_examination: Well-oriented and hyperpyrexic. Cutaneous examination revealed generalized maculopapular and bullous eruptions over the face, neck, and trunk. Ophthalmic examination showed bilateral acute conjunctivitis and subconjunctival hemorrhages. Intraoral examination revealed an edentulous patient with multiple tender hemorrhagic ulcerations across the buccal mucosa, soft palate, and buccal vestibule, along with crusted hemorrhagic erosions on the upper and lower vermilion lips.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission laboratory tests showed WBC 4,860 cells/mm3 (normal 4,000–11,000), hemoglobin 11.9 g/dL (normal 12–17), platelets 208 x 10^9/L (normal 137–367 x 10^9/L), elevated ESR 36 mm/h (normal 0–14 mm/h), random blood glucose 186 mg/dL (normal 80–120 mg/dL), and normal urinalysis and serum chemistry. Chest X-ray showed no active tuberculous lesions.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission CD4+ T-cell count was 470 cells/µL (normal 200–1,347 cells/µL).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Nevirapine/HAART-induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS) with severe mucocutaneous and ocular involvement in a 50-year-old male with HIV-1 infection (prior viral load 109,000 copies/mL, admission CD4+ count 470 cells/µL) and concurrent anti-tuberculosis therapy. Management consisted of immediate discontinuation of HAART (zidovudine/lamivudine/nevirapine), intravenous fluid hydration (5% dextrose), systemic intravenous dexamethasone (2 mL of 4 mg/mL), topical 2% lignocaine anesthetic gel and liquid paraffin for oral/lip ulcerations, and topical 0.1% dexamethasone ophthalmic drops for conjunctivitis. Cutaneous and oral lesions healed within 2 weeks, with complete resolution of all mucosal lesions confirmed at 12-week follow-up.
